source_title: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance — stick insect
facts: Some stick insects can reproduce without males, producing daughters from unfertilised eggs.
Stick insects sometimes sway as they walk, resembling twigs moving in the wind.
Some stick insects flash bright wings, then hide them as they drop into leaf litter.
Stick insect eggs can resemble seeds.
Ants carry some stick insect eggs underground to eat an attached nutrient packet.
Stick insect young can hatch safely inside an ant nest and later walk out.
Young stick insects resemble miniature adults rather than going through a caterpillar stage.
Some stick insects spray irritating defensive chemicals.
Stick insects may eat their shed skins, recycling nutrients and removing evidence of their presence.
A stick insect's visual disguise is less useful against a hunting bat's sound-based senses.

source_title: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance — tarantula
facts: Many American tarantulas flick irritating hairs toward threats.
Tarantulas use silk for homes and moulting mats, not just prey-catching traps.
A tarantula often lies on its back while shedding its old outer skeleton.
A shed tarantula skin can look remarkably like a second spider.
Tarantulas liquefy prey tissues before consuming them.
Some male tarantulas have leg hooks that help hold a female's fangs away during mating.
Female tarantulas can live much longer than males.
A mother tarantula guards her eggs inside a silk cocoon.
Tarantula hawk wasps paralyse spiders and leave them as food for their larvae.
The king baboon spider can make a hissing sound by rubbing its mouthparts together.

source_title: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance — scorpion
facts: Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light because of fluorescent material in their outer covering.
Scorpions are arachnids with eight legs, not insects.
Newborn scorpions ride on their mother's back until their first moult.
Scorpions give birth to live young.
Scorpions use comb-like structures beneath their bodies to sense their surroundings.
Scorpions digest prey externally and consume it as liquid.
Scorpion courtship often involves a pair holding pincers and moving together.
Some scorpions raise their bodies off hot ground to cool their undersides.
A scorpion's apparent tail is actually an extension of its abdomen.
Some scorpions can go many months without food when water remains available.

source_title: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance — dung beetle
facts: Not all dung beetles roll balls: some tunnel under dung and others live inside it.
Dung beetles return nutrients to soil by burying animal waste.
Some dung beetles provide their young with a buried ball of food.
Some dung beetle parents stay with their developing larvae for months.
Adult dung beetles often feed on the liquid portion of fresh dung.
Dung beetles locate fresh droppings using sensitive antennae.
Australia introduced dung beetles to help process cattle manure.
Ancient Egyptians associated scarab beetles with the rising sun.
Burrowing owls sometimes use dung as bait to attract beetles.
A Peruvian dung beetle species hunts millipedes instead of relying on manure.
